column1: # tests/budgets.tsv (W160): every `make test-long` command, its wall-time budget in
# seconds at EFS_TEST_JOBS=8: Task T maximum of three host medians (three clean
# gates each on intel1/xorinox/fstor007), times 1.25 rounded up to 5 s. Evidence:
# re-measured every row on amd and node9900 (three 8-job gates each, passing runs only) with
# intel2's wave 42/44 gates and earlier measured notes as further evidence: the "BN:" note
# gives the slowest median that sets the row. The pool slots and historical
# reason prefixes are retained; above the bound
# in tests/test_make_test_recipe.py, why. Slots weigh disk use, not CPU (the daemon
# tests use 0.15-0.3 CPU each but their stores fsync on one disk): 6 the report
# step-down test's historical reservation; timing/setup-sensitive cases listed in
# the runner's EXCLUSIVE set now run alone, independent of fitted cost. Their slot
# values and reason prefixes are retained as provenance; old first-window claims
# do not override current runner isolation. 3 a test whose driver or writers fsync
# for most of its run (B growth, stop
# progress), so at most two overlap; 2 a daemon test that writes a moderate set with fsync;
# 1 a test that mostly waits on daemon timers (member-down detection, unmount fences,
# the slow member's deliberate delays) or a CPU-bound process. scripts/make_test_summary.sh starts the
# largest budgets first and lists OVERBUDGET commands; tests/test_make_test_recipe.py
# bounds the budgets and the budgeted gate time. Evidence: docs/status/gate-speed-20261025.md.
